meta.description: From identity verification to spending: the five steps to obtaining and using crypto-collateralized credit on Hentsch Credit.

HowItWorks.title: How it works
HowItWorks.description: From identity verification to spending, in five steps.

kyc.title: 1. Identity verification (KYC)
kyc.description: By invitation only: your identity is verified before any access to deposits or credit, with no exceptions.

deposit.title: 2. Deposit your collateral
deposit.description: Stablecoins, tokenized precious or industrial metals, or ETH, on the Ethereum network.

credit.title: 3. Credit granted automatically
credit.description: 350% of the deposited amount, unlocked as soon as your request is approved (minus a one-time 2% origination fee).

spend.title: 4. Spend with your card
spend.description: Use your credit line internally or directly on your bank card.

repay.title: 5. Repay to unlock your collateral
repay.description: Up to 60% automatically repaid by your collateral's yield; the rest through your own contribution. Conversely, a sharp drop in your collateral's value may trigger its liquidation.

HowItWorks.feesNote: The detail of actual rates and fees lives on the <pricing>Pricing</pricing> page, and the detail of automatic repayment, including the liquidation risk in the event of a sharp drop in your collateral, on the <yield>Yield</yield> page.

kyc.title: 1. Identity verification
kyc.body: Access is granted by invitation only. Once your account opening request is accepted, an account and a temporary password are communicated to you offline, then your identity is verified before any other operation. Until this status is confirmed, generating a deposit address and any credit request are technically blocked, not merely discouraged.

deposit.title: 2. Depositing the collateral
deposit.body: Depending on the asset chosen, the deposit address provided is either individual (credited automatically upon on-chain confirmation) or shared among clients (you declare your deposit, and an advisor validates it manually once the funds are actually received). The corresponding credit is issued automatically as soon as the available balance reaches the requested amount, with no further manual action on our part.

credit.title: 3. Credit issuance
credit.body: 350% of the deposited amount, at the rate in effect at the time of the lock: a position already locked always keeps that rate, even if the ratio subsequently changes for new clients. Origination fees (2%) are charged once, on the credit issued, not on your collateral.

usage.title: 4. Using the credit
usage.body: The credit granted is only a ceiling: no interest or repayment is due until you actually use it (card payment, internal use). It is a revolving credit line, not a loan paid out all at once into your available balance.

repayment.title: 5. Repayment
repayment.body: Two channels, daily and automatic for the first: the real appreciation of your collateral (up to 60% of the credit issued), and your own contribution for the rest. Full repayment releases your collateral, which becomes withdrawable again. Conversely, a severe depreciation of the collateral (50% since entry) triggers its liquidation, without erasing the credit already used.

kycRejected.question: What happens if my KYC is rejected?
kycRejected.answer: No financial operation is possible until the status is verified. In the event of rejection, the company may refuse, suspend, or close the account concerned, particularly in case of doubt about the declared identity.

approvalDelay.question: How long does approval of a credit request take?
approvalDelay.answer: It varies depending on back-office workload: a request goes through a manual validation queue before it can receive a deposit. The credit itself is issued automatically upon receipt of funds, with no additional delay once the request is approved.

earlyWithdrawal.question: Can I withdraw my collateral before repaying everything?
earlyWithdrawal.answer: No. Locked collateral remains blocked until the corresponding credit used has been fully repaid. Only the available balance, excluding locked collateral, can be freely withdrawn at any time.

Accessibility.title: Accessibility statement
Accessibility.intro: H. Hentsch Asset Management SA strives to make the Hentsch Credit platform usable by as many people as possible. This statement describes the actual state of progress, without claiming a compliance level that has not been verified by a formal audit.

s1.title: 1. Compliance status
s1.body: The site has not yet undergone a formal accessibility audit (of the RGAA or WCAG type). It cannot therefore be declared compliant with a specific level. Efforts are nonetheless already applied in the design: semantic page structure, heading hierarchy, color contrasts designed for readability, and keyboard navigation possible on the main journeys (login, account request, account consultation).

s2.title: 2. Known limitations
s2.item1: Certain charts and market data tables do not yet offer a complete text equivalent for screen readers;
s2.item2: No adversarial audit has been conducted by a third-party organization specializing in digital accessibility;
s2.item3: Certain third-party content (for example webhooks and external provider interfaces integrated into the platform) is not under the direct control of {legalName}.

s3.title: 3. Reporting an issue
s3.body: If you encounter a difficulty accessing content or a feature of the platform, please report it to the contact below, specifying the page concerned and, if possible, the assistive technology used.

s4.title: 4. Recourse
s4.body: In the absence of a satisfactory response within a reasonable time, you can file a complaint under the conditions described on the <link>Regulation</link> page, section 6.

meta.title: Archives · Hentsch Credit
meta.description: The evolution of the credit ratio, accepted assets, and mechanisms of the Hentsch Credit platform since its launch.

Archives.title: Archives
Archives.description: The evolution of the platform's main rules since its launch, in chronological order.

nonRetroactivity.title: Non-retroactivity of changes to terms
nonRetroactivity.detail: A change to the credit ratio, rate, or threshold never applies to a position already locked: it retains the conditions granted to it at the time of its creation, until repayment or maturity. This principle has never changed since the platform's launch.

step2.title: First increase in the ratio
step2.detail: 75% → 150% of the amount pledged, for new locks.

step3.title: Second increase in the ratio
step3.detail: 150% → 200% of the amount pledged, for new locks.

step4.title: Current credit ratio
step4.detail: 200% → 350% of the amount pledged, for new locks.

step5.title: Extension of accepted assets
step5.detail: Addition of ETH and SHIB, then of tokenized silver (KAG), in addition to stablecoins.

step6.title: Extension to industrial metals and commodities
step6.detail: Addition of platinum (XPT), palladium (XPD), copper (XCU), and synthetic oil (WTI), as part of the RWA strategy.

step7.title: Automatic repayment through collateral yield
step7.detail: Introduction of automatic repayment through the collateral's real appreciation, capped at 60% of the credit issued; the remainder is still the client's responsibility.

step8.title: Indicative yield target on industrial RWA assets
step8.detail: Addition of an indicative annualized target of 8 to 14% on platinum, palladium, copper, and synthetic oil only. This target remains indicative: it is neither guaranteed nor used in the calculation of the credit granted.

step9.title: Introduction of the liquidation mechanism
step9.detail: Introduction of an alert threshold (30% depreciation of the collateral since entry) and a liquidation threshold (50%). Details are on the Yield page and in the terms and conditions, section 7.

step10.title: Move to an automatically calculated estimated yield
step10.detail: The client credit simulators now calculate the estimated yield, monthly payment, and first repayment date based on actual performance over 12 months, rather than asking the client to enter an estimate.

Archives.note: The values currently in effect (ratio, rates, fees, yield cap, liquidation thresholds) are detailed with their exact figures on the <link>Pricing</link> page. This archives page only traces the history of changes, not the terms applicable to your current position.

Cookies.title: Cookie policy
Cookies.intro: This page describes the cookies actually set by the Hentsch Credit platform and why no preference center is offered.

s1.title: 1. What the platform sets
s1.body: Only one cookie is used, a session cookie, strictly necessary for the service to function: it keeps you authenticated while you browse the client area. It is deleted when your session or browser is closed.

s2.title: 2. What the platform does not set
s2.item2: No third-party audience measurement cookie (analytics, statistics);

s3.title: 3. Why there is no "manage my cookies"
s3.body: A preference center makes sense when a site sets non-essential cookies (advertising, audience measurement) that require your prior consent and a way to withdraw it. The platform sets none of these: there is therefore no preference to enable or disable beyond your own browser's settings. Should this change one day, this page will be updated and a genuine preference center will be offered, rather than a button with no real effect.

s4.title: 4. Control from your browser
s4.body: You can block or delete the session cookie at any time from your browser settings. Blocking this particular cookie will log you out of the client area: it is a functional cookie, not a tracker, and it has no other role.

s5.title: 5. Contact
s5.body: For any question regarding this policy, contact the data protection officer at {dpo}. The processing of other personal data is described in the <link>privacy policy</link>.

meta.title: Terms and conditions · Hentsch Credit
meta.description: Hentsch Credit's terms and conditions of use: credit, collateral, repayment, liquidation, and fees.

Terms.title: Terms and conditions
Terms.intro: These terms and conditions govern access to and use of the Hentsch Credit platform, a credit service secured by digital assets, offered to a restricted number of the company's clients by invitation. By opening an account, the client declares having read and accepted them.

s1.title: 1. Purpose
s1.body: {tradingName} allows a verified, previously invited client to deposit stablecoins or tokenized gold as collateral (a "pledge") and, in return, obtain a credit line usable internally and on an associated bank card. The service is provided by {legalName}, an independent asset manager (IAM) within the meaning of FinIA, in collaboration with licensed third-party depositary and custody institutions (see section 5).

s2.title: 2. Restricted access and eligibility
s2.body: The platform is not open to the public. Access is reserved for a list of clients determined by {legalName}, by invitation, as part of an existing wealth management relationship. Opening an account, generating a deposit address, any collateral deposit, and any credit grant are further subject to prior verification of the client's identity ("KYC"). Until the client's verification status is confirmed, these operations are refused. The company reserves the right to refuse, suspend, or close an account in the event of failure or doubt regarding this verification, or suspicion of fraud, money laundering, or terrorist financing.

s3.title: 3. Assets accepted as collateral
s3.body: The following stablecoins are accepted as collateral, valued at par (1:1 USD): DAI, USDT, USDC; the following euro-pegged stablecoin, valued at the live spot price: dEURO; the following tokenized precious metals, also valued at the live spot price: XAUT (gold), KAG (silver); the following tokenized industrial metals and commodities, valued at the live spot price: XPT (platinum), XPD (palladium), XCU (copper), WTI (synthetic oil); as well as the following native cryptocurrencies, valued at the live spot price and subject to their own volatility: ETH, SHIB. These assets are accepted exclusively on the Ethereum network. For certain assets, the deposit address provided is individual to each client; for others, it is shared among clients and the declared deposit is subject to manual validation before being credited. The list of accepted assets, supported networks, or the address mechanism applicable to each asset may be changed at any time, without retroactive effect on positions already established.

s4.title: 4. Credit mechanism and collateral ratio
s4.body1: When collateral is locked, credit is granted equal to 350% of the amount pledged, at the rate in effect at the time of that lock. The account's total purchasing power is calculated as follows:
s4.formula: Total purchasing power = Available balance + Locked collateral + Credit granted − Credit used
s4.body2: The applicable collateral ratio is the one in effect at the time of each new lock. Any subsequent change to this ratio does not retroactively affect credit already granted for collateral locked earlier: that credit remains vested under the conditions of its time.
s4.body3: Credit issued on eligible collateral (tokenized precious metals, tokenized industrial metals and commodities, ETH) may be repaid up to a maximum of 60% through the real appreciation observed on that collateral, applied automatically to the credit used. The remaining 40% must be repaid through the client's own contribution (an explicit deposit or transfer). This cap applies to the amount of credit issued when the position was opened and is not recalculated in the event of a subsequent change to the credit ratio.
s4.body4: An indicative yield target (currently 8 to 14% per year) is communicated for information purposes on tokenized industrial metals and commodities (platinum, palladium, copper, synthetic oil): it reflects the target of the company's own treasury strategy on these assets (arbitrage, collateralized lending, liquidity provision), and not a guaranteed or contractual rate. This target has no effect whatsoever on the calculation of the client's credit, which remains governed exclusively by the mechanism described in the preceding paragraph.

s6.title: 6. Collateral lock and withdrawal
s6.body: The amount pledged and locked cannot be withdrawn until the corresponding credit used has been fully repaid. Only the available balance, excluding locked collateral, may be freely withdrawn at any time, subject to applicable compliance controls.

s7.title: 7. Liquidation of collateral
s7.intro: Collateral whose value fluctuates with the market (tokenized precious metals, tokenized industrial metals and commodities, ETH) is subject to daily monitoring of its value, compared against its value at the time of the lock:
s7.item1: in the event of a depreciation of at least 30% from this entry value, an alert is recorded on the account, with no other effect;
s7.item2: in the event of a depreciation of at least 50%, the collateral is automatically removed from the account (liquidated) at its entry value.
s7.body: Liquidation of collateral does not extinguish credit already used under that collateral: that credit remains fully owed by the client, no longer covered by the collateral originally constituted. Liquidated collateral cannot be restored, even if the price of the asset concerned subsequently recovers. The thresholds mentioned above may be changed at any time, without retroactive effect on the assessment of a depreciation already recorded.

s8.title: 8. Bank card and use of credit
s8.body: A bank card, issued by a licensed third-party partner, may be linked to the account to use the credit line granted, within the limit of available credit (credit granted minus credit already used). Any transaction exceeding this limit is declined. The specific conditions for issuing, using, and blocking the card are set out in the special conditions associated with it.

s9.title: 9. Repayment
s9.body: The client may repay all or part of the credit used at any time. Full repayment of the credit used under a given collateral releases that collateral, which becomes withdrawable again. The repayment simulators made available on the platform (flexible projection, fixed installments) are provided for indicative purposes only: they rely on an estimated yield based on past performance, which does not predict future performance, and constitute neither a contractual commitment nor an enforceable payment schedule.

s10.title: 10. Fees
s10.body: The fees and rates currently applied are: origination fees of 2.0%, charged once on the credit issued at the time the collateral is locked; collateral custody fees of 0.5% per year, on the amount of locked collateral; and interest on the credit used of 13.5% per year in USD (12.0% per year in EUR), made up of a monetary reference rate (SOFR for USD, EURIBOR for EUR) and a risk premium of 8.5 points, justified by the platform's high credit ratio (350%). Up-to-date details of these fees are on the platform's Pricing page. These rates may be updated at any time, without retroactive effect on positions already established: the rate structure fixed at the time a position is locked remains vested until its repayment or maturity.

s11.title: 11. Risks
s11.intro: The client acknowledges and accepts the risks inherent to digital assets, notably:
s11.item1: the volatility of assets valued at spot price (tokenized gold), which may affect the value of the collateral and the account's total purchasing power;
s11.item2: the risk of collateral liquidation in the event of severe depreciation (see section 7), which does not extinguish credit already used;
s11.item3: counterparty risk and operational risk related to the depositary institutions and third-party custody providers mentioned in section 5;
s11.item4: regulatory risk related to the evolution of the legal framework applicable to digital assets and stablecoins.
s11.body: These terms constitute neither investment advice nor a recommendation to buy, sell, or hold any digital asset whatsoever.

s12.title: 12. Termination
s12.body: The client may close their account at any time, subject to full repayment of any credit used. The company may suspend or terminate access to the service in the event of a breach of these terms, suspicion of fraud or money laundering, or for any legal or regulatory reason.

s13.title: 13. Liability
s13.body: The company implements reasonable means to ensure the availability and security of the platform, without guaranteeing a total absence of interruption. Its liability cannot be engaged in the event of force majeure, a malfunction of a blockchain network, or a third-party provider beyond its control, within the limits permitted by applicable Swiss law.

s14.title: 14. Amendment of the terms and conditions
s14.body: The company may amend these terms and conditions at any time, subject to prior notice to the client through the usual means of communication. Amendments have no retroactive effect on credit positions already established, unless otherwise required by law.

s15.title: 15. Governing law and jurisdiction
s15.body: These terms and conditions are governed by Swiss law. Any dispute relating to their validity, interpretation, or performance falls under the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of {jurisdiction}, subject to applicable mandatory legal provisions.

Privacy.title: Privacy policy
Privacy.intro: This policy describes how H. Hentsch Asset Management SA collects, uses, and protects the personal data of Hentsch Credit clients, a platform reserved for a restricted clientele, in accordance with the Swiss federal act on data protection (nFADP) and, where applicable, the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR).

s1.title: 1. Data controller
s1.compliance: Compliant with the Swiss FADP and GDPR.

s2.title: 2. Data collected
s2.item1: Identification and contact data (name, email, contact details);
s2.item2: Identity verification (KYC) documents and data submitted when opening an account;
s2.item3: Data relating to deposit addresses, on-chain transactions, and operations carried out on the platform (deposits, collateral locks, credit grants, repayments, card payments);
s2.item4: Technical connection data for the platform (logs, session identifiers).

s3.title: 3. Purposes and legal basis
s3.item1: Performance of the contractual relationship: opening and managing the account, granting and monitoring credit, issuing and managing the associated bank card;
s3.item2: Compliance with legal and regulatory obligations: identity verification (KYC), anti-money laundering and counter-terrorist financing (AMLA), retention of accounting records;
s3.item4: Communication with the client regarding their account and operations.

s4.title: 4. Partners and subcontractors
s4.intro: To perform the service, {legalName} uses specialized providers, which process certain data on its behalf and under its instructions, or which act as separate controllers for asset custody:
s4.item1Body: custody of clients' cash and securities (see legal notice, section 3);
s4.item2Body: secure custody of stablecoins and tokenized gold deposited as collateral;
s4.item4Body: checking the client's identity and compliance status;
s4.item5Body: detection of on-chain deposits and real-time asset prices.
s4.outro: The name, exact role, and country of establishment of each provider used in production are communicated to the client upon request to the service indicated in section 1.

s5.title: 5. Retention period
s5.body: Data relating to clients and their operations is retained for the duration of the management relationship, then for the period required by the applicable legal retention obligations (accounting documents and supporting evidence of transactions in particular).

s6.title: 6. International transfers
s6.body: Some providers mentioned in section 4 may process data outside Switzerland. In that case, {legalName} implements the appropriate safeguards required by Swiss data protection legislation (contractual clauses, an adequacy decision, or an equivalent mechanism).

s7.title: 7. Your rights
s7.body: Subject to the restrictions provided for by law (in particular the applicable legal retention obligations), the client has a right of access, rectification, erasure, and objection with respect to their personal data. These rights may be exercised by writing to the address indicated in section 1.

s8.title: 8. Cookies and trackers
s8.body: The platform uses only cookies strictly necessary for its operation (session authentication, display preferences). No advertising or third-party audience measurement cookie is set without the client's prior consent. Details are given in the <link>cookie policy</link>.

s9.title: 9. Special case of prospects (account opening requests)
s9.body: Individuals who submit an account opening request without yet being clients (via the Request an account page) provide identification and contact data as well as information about their investment project. This data is processed for the sole purpose of reviewing the request. If the request does not result in a wealth management relationship, it is retained for a limited period, necessary for follow-up of the file, then deleted; if accepted, it is incorporated into the client file and follows the retention rules described in section 5.

s10.title: 10. Security
s10.body: {legalName} implements appropriate technical and organizational measures (encryption, access control, distributed locks on financial operations) to protect personal data against unauthorized access, loss, or alteration.

meta.title: Risk management and asset custody · Hentsch Credit
meta.description: How Hentsch Credit manages asset custody, collateral valuation, and the liquidation mechanism.

RiskManagement.title: Risk management and asset custody
RiskManagement.intro: H. Hentsch Asset Management SA does not execute stock exchange orders on behalf of third parties and therefore does not publish an execution policy or best selection report within the meaning of financial markets regulation. This page describes instead the actual risk management practices applied to the Hentsch Credit platform.

s1.title: 1. Nature of the activity
s1.body: {legalName} acts as an independent asset manager (IAM): it grants crypto-collateralized credit to its clients, against collateral deposited by them, and manages a treasury strategy on tokenized industrial metals and commodities with its own capital. It does not execute any stock exchange order on behalf of its clients and manages no discretionary securities portfolio in their name.

s2.title: 2. Custody and segregation of assets
s2.body: Assets deposited as collateral by clients are never used in the company's treasury strategy: the two flows are distinct and never meet at any point. Details of the treasury strategy are on the <link>RWA Strategy</link> page, section "Governance & fund segregation".

s3.title: 3. Collateral valuation
s3.body: The value of the deposited collateral is determined from real-time market prices (spot price for tokenized gold, tokenized industrial metals, ETH; 1:1 parity with the dollar for USD stablecoins; spot price for the euro-pegged stablecoin), with no margin or discretionary adjustment applied by the company. This valuation is used both to calculate the credit granted at the time of the lock and for the daily depreciation monitoring described below.

s4.title: 4. Collateral liquidation mechanism
s4.body: An automatic daily check compares the current value of the collateral to its entry value (at the time of the lock). A 30% depreciation triggers an alert visible on the client's account; a 50% depreciation triggers liquidation of the collateral. Credit already used is not erased by liquidation: it becomes an unsecured claim. Full details, with a worked example, are on the <yieldLink>Yield</yieldLink> page and in the <termsLink>terms and conditions</termsLink>, section 7.

s5.title: 5. Conflicts of interest
s5.body: The company never takes a position contrary to that of its clients on the assets they deposit as collateral: it only receives that collateral, calculates the corresponding credit, and, where applicable, liquidates it according to thresholds set in advance and applied automatically and identically to all clients. The company's treasury strategy (industrial metals and commodities) is funded by its own capital, never by assets deposited by clients.

s6.title: 6. Oversight and audit
s6.body: The risk parameters in effect (credit ratio, rates, liquidation thresholds) are centralized in the platform's credit engine and are subject to an automated test suite with every change. Any change to these parameters is logged and never applies retroactively to a position already locked. Details of the history of these changes are on the <link>Archives</link> page.

LegalNotice.title: Legal notice
LegalNotice.intro: Legal information relating to the publisher and operator of the Hentsch Credit site and platform, in accordance with applicable Swiss law. Platform reserved for a restricted clientele, by invitation only: it is not open to the public and does not constitute a public offering.

s2.title: 2. Regulatory status and supervision
s2.body: {legalName} is an independent asset manager (IAM) within the meaning of the Federal Act on Financial Institutions (FinIA), and not a banking institution. Regulation.title: Regulatory framework
Regulation.intro: This page details the Swiss legal and regulatory framework applicable to Hentsch Credit, in addition to the legal notice.

s1.title: 1. Applicable legal framework
s1.intro: The activity of {legalName} is notably governed by:
s1.item1: the Federal Act on Financial Institutions (FinIA) and its ordinance (FinIO), applicable to independent asset managers;
s1.item2: the Federal Act on Financial Services (FinSA) and its ordinance (FinSO), relating to the provision of financial services and client classification;
s1.item3: the Anti-Money Laundering Act (AMLA), relating to due diligence and vigilance obligations;
s1.item4: the Federal Act on Data Protection (nFADP) and, where applicable, the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR).

s2.title: 2. Status of the operator
s2.body1: {legalName} is an independent asset manager (IAM) within the meaning of FinIA: it holds no banking license and accepts no public deposit of funds in its own name.
s2.body2: The SO licenses and supervises the wealth management activity, monitors compliance with legal obligations (including AMLA), and may impose measures in the event of a breach. Details of the publisher's identity are in the <link>legal notice</link>.

s4.title: 4. Client classification (FinSA)
s4.body: FinSA distinguishes three categories of clients (retail, professional, and institutional), to which correspond different levels of information and protection. {tradingName}'s clientele is classified as {classification} within the meaning of FinSA, the category offering the highest level of protection and information. Access nonetheless remains reserved for a restricted list of clients, by invitation, as part of an existing wealth management relationship with {legalName}.

s5.title: 5. Anti-money laundering (AMLA)
s5.body: In accordance with AMLA, access to the platform, the generation of a deposit address, and any credit grant are subject to prior verification of the client's identity and the economic origin of the assets concerned. {legalName} applies enhanced due diligence measures in the presence of indications of money laundering or terrorist financing, and complies with reporting obligations provided for by law where applicable.

s6.title: 6. Complaints and mediation
s6.body: Any complaint relating to the service may be addressed to the contact indicated below. Failing an amicable resolution, the client may, under the conditions provided for by FinSA, refer the matter to the mediation body under which {legalName} falls: {mediationBody}.

meta.title: Collateral yield · Hentsch Credit
meta.description: How gold, silver, and ETH deposited as collateral automatically repay up to 60% of your credit, and the liquidation risk in the event of a sharp drop.

Yield.title: The only collateral that repays part of your credit for you
Yield.description: Gold, silver, and ETH generate a real yield, automatically reinjected into your credit, up to 60% repaid without a second thought.
Yield.eligibleAssetsIntro: Eight assets benefit from the same real automatic repayment-by-appreciation mechanism, not just the gold, silver, and ETH highlighted above.

table.notEligible: Not eligible (fixed value or too volatile*)

Yield.shibNote: * SHIB is not a stablecoin but remains excluded from the mechanism: its volatility is considered too high to support a reliable recurring repayment.
Yield.dualMechanismNote: Industrial metals and commodities therefore combine two distinct mechanisms: the real automatic repayment described on this page (identical to gold, silver, and ETH), and an indicative yield target specific to the bank's treasury strategy on these assets, presented separately and never guaranteed.
Yield.performanceIntro: The real prices of the yield-generating assets, over the last 365 days (the maximum available via our market data provider, with no commitment as to their future performance).

example.p1: You deposit $2,000 of tokenized gold (XAUT), at a price of $2,400 per ounce: your collateral represents about 0.833 ounces. At the 350% ratio, credit of $7,000 is granted to you, and the automatic repayment-by-yield cap is therefore $4,200 (60% of $7,000).
example.p2: The gold price rises to $2,500 per ounce: the observed appreciation ($100 × 0.833 ounces ≈ $83) is automatically applied to your credit used, the very day it is recorded. This mechanism repeats with every subsequent price increase, until the $4,200 cap is reached.
example.p3: If the price then falls, nothing is taken back from you: the appreciation already applied remains vested in your credit (a "ratchet" that only ever moves upward). However, no new automatic repayment occurs until the price exceeds the level already reached.
example.p4: Once the 60% cap is exhausted, the remaining credit balance (at least 40%, here $2,800) must be repaid through an explicit payment on your part (deposit or transfer), as with any other credit.

Yield.timelineIntro: The same example, extended: the gold price continues to rise over several months, until it reaches the 60% cap.
Yield.timelineNote: In month 2, the price falls: no repayment occurs that month, but the $83 already applied in month 1 remains vested (ratchet). Once the $4,200 cap is reached in month 11, no further automatic repayment occurs on this position, even if the price continues to rise.

liquidation.p1: The mechanism above benefits from a rising price. A decline is handled separately, through a distinct mechanism: the value of your collateral is compared daily to its entry value (the one recorded at the time of the lock), not to the last price that triggered a repayment.
liquidation.p2: In the event of a depreciation of at least 30% since entry, an alert appears on your account, with no other effect. At 50% depreciation, your collateral is automatically removed from the account (liquidated) at its entry value. The credit you had already used is not erased as a result: it remains fully owed, no longer secured by any collateral. Liquidated collateral cannot be restored, even if the price subsequently recovers.
liquidation.p3: The contractual details of this mechanism are in our <link>terms and conditions, section 7</link>.

liquidationExample.intro: Let's take the same $2,000 gold deposit at $2,400 per ounce ($7,000 of credit granted), but this time the gold price falls instead of rising:
liquidationExample.item1: at $1,680 per ounce (-30%): an alert appears on the account, with no other effect;
liquidationExample.item2: at $1,200 per ounce (-50%): the collateral is liquidated. The $2,000 of collateral and the $7,000 of credit granted are removed from the account. If you had already used $1,500 of that credit (card, internal spending), that $1,500 remains owed, with no collateral behind it anymore.

guaranteed.question: Is the yield guaranteed?
guaranteed.answer: No. It depends entirely on the actual movement of your collateral's price. If the price never rises above your entry price, no automatic repayment occurs: you then repay the full amount through your own contribution, exactly as with a stablecoin.

stablecoins.question: Why don't stablecoins (USDT, USDC, DAI…) generate any?
stablecoins.answer: A stablecoin remains, by design, pegged 1:1 to the dollar: by definition, it has no appreciation to realize. Repaying it nonetheless remains just as simple, through your own contribution.

frequency.question: How often is the automatic repayment calculated?
frequency.answer: Daily, based on the live spot price of your asset, with no action on your part, and visible in your transaction history under the label "Repayment by collateral yield."

ratchet.question: Does the "ratchet" protect me if the price falls?
ratchet.answer: It only protects repayments already applied: they remain vested, whatever happens afterward. It does not protect against liquidation, which is triggered relative to your collateral's entry value, not relative to the ratchet (see "The reverse risk" above).

multipleAssets.question: If I deposit several different assets, how does it work?
multipleAssets.answer: Each credit request commits to a single collateral asset, fixed at the time the deposit address is generated. To deposit a second asset, you submit a new request: each position then follows its own appreciation, its own 60% cap, and its own liquidation risk, independently of the others.

history.question: Can I see the history of my automatic repayments?
history.answer: Yes, in your account's transaction history, under the label "Repayment by collateral yield" (a movement distinct from a manual repayment, to remain separately auditable).

meta.title: RWA investment strategy · Hentsch Credit
meta.description: Hentsch Credit's treasury strategy on tokenized industrial metals: cash and carry arbitrage, triangular lending, and liquidity provision.

RwaStrategy.title: Our investment strategy on industrial metals
RwaStrategy.intro: Beyond precious metals, the bank now accepts tokenized industrial metals and commodities as collateral, and deploys its own treasury strategy on these assets. Here, in full transparency, is how it works and the action plan followed.
RwaStrategy.apyTargetNote: Target of the bank's own treasury strategy on these assets, not a guarantee, and with no effect whatsoever on the calculation of your credit. The automatic repayment of your credit remains the one described above: the real appreciation of your collateral, capped at 60%.

cashCarry.title: Cash & Carry Arbitrage
cashCarry.description: Purchase of the tokenized metal on the spot market, simultaneous sale of an equivalent futures contract: the position is price-risk neutral and captures the financing spread (contango).

triangular.title: Collateralization & triangular lending
triangular.description: The tokenized metal is deposited as collateral (prudent LTV, 50% maximum) with an institutional protocol, to borrow stablecoins reinvested in low-risk treasury funds.

liquidity.title: Selected liquidity provision
liquidity.description: A minority share of the capital feeds targeted liquidity pools, remunerated by a fraction of the transaction fees paid by market participants.

caseStudy.title: How these figures are obtained
caseStudy.intro: An illustrative example of a $10M treasury deployment on Platinum, at the bank's scale, not at the scale of your individual collateral.
caseStudy.reallocationNote: By reallocating part of the treasury toward liquidity provision (Pillar C), this net yield can rise to a target of 10.2%, at the top end of the indicative 8 to 14% range shown above, with no additional leverage or guarantee of results.

phase1.title: Structuring & compliance
phase1.detail: Legal framework, selection of licensed depositaries, issuer audits.

phase2.title: Pilot project
phase2.detail: A $5M pilot allocation on Platinum, first arbitrage circuits.

phase3.title: Scale-up
phase3.detail: Capital extended to $25M, expansion to Palladium and Copper.

phase4.title: Industrialization
phase4.detail: Real-time reporting and end-to-end accounting integration.

counterparty.mitigation: Bimonthly reserve audits (Proof of Reserve) by independent firms.

smartContract.mitigation: Protocols audited multiple times exclusively, covered by institutional insurance.

liquidity.mitigation: Direct buyback agreement with physical issuers, maximum 48-hour notice.

liquidation.mitigation: Strict over-collateralization ratio (LTV ≤ 50%) with automated rebalancing.

capital.title: Capital deployed
capital.body: This strategy is run on the bank's own treasury, never on assets deposited as collateral by clients. A client's collateral is used exclusively to secure their own credit (see Yield); it is never lent out or committed to the arbitrage or market making described above.

supervision.title: Supervision
supervision.body: Overseen by the Financial Markets Division, reported to the Investment Committee and Executive Management at each phase change (see roadmap above), with daily internal monitoring of performance against the indicative target shown.

usedForStrategy.question: Is my collateral used for this strategy?
usedForStrategy.answer: No. Your collateral remains exclusively allocated to your own credit. This strategy relates to the bank's own treasury, a separate pool of capital.

loss.question: What happens if the strategy loses money?
loss.answer: The loss is absorbed by the bank's treasury, with no effect whatsoever on client accounts or on credit already granted: this risk is never transferred to the client.

targetReached.question: Has the 8 to 14% target already been reached?
targetReached.answer: It is a medium-term target, not a result guaranteed month by month: see the case study above for a detailed example of the net yield calculation.

whyIndustrialOnly.question: Why do only industrial metals have this target?
whyIndustrialOnly.answer: Gold, silver, and ETH already benefit from the real automatic repayment described on the Yield page. This indicative target is specific to the treasury strategy on industrial assets, a distinct and additional mechanism.

meta.title: Pricing · Hentsch Credit
meta.description: The actual rates and fees applied by Hentsch Credit: credit ratio, interest, origination fees, and liquidation thresholds, with no surprises.

Pricing.title: Our pricing, no surprises
Pricing.description: The rates and fees actually applied by the platform, fixed at the time your collateral is locked.

ratio.label: Credit ratio
ratio.detail: Of the amount pledged, at the rate in effect at the time of the lock.

interestRate.label: Annual interest rate
interestRate.detail: Reference rate (SOFR/EURIBOR) plus a risk premium of 8.5 points, on the credit used.

originationFees.label: Origination fees
originationFees.detail: Charged once, on the credit issued, at the time the collateral is locked.

custodyFees.label: Collateral custody fees
custodyFees.detail: On the amount of locked collateral, for as long as the position remains active.

positionDuration.label: Position term
positionDuration.detail: Renewable; the collateral remains locked until the credit used is repaid.

automaticRepayment.label: Automatic repayment
automaticRepayment.detail: Through the real appreciation of the collateral (gold, silver, ETH, industrial metals). The remaining 40% is repaid through your own contribution.

liquidationThresholds.label: Collateral liquidation thresholds
liquidationThresholds.detail: Depreciation from the entry value: 30% triggers an alert, 50% liquidates the collateral (credit already used remains owed). Details on the Yield page.

Pricing.nonRetroactivityNote: Any subsequent change to one of these rates applies only to new locks: a position already open retains the rate structure applied to it at the time of its creation, until its repayment or maturity.
Pricing.contractualDetail: The full contractual details of these fees are in our <link>terms and conditions</link>.
Pricing.exampleTitle: Example of total cost over 12 months
Pricing.exampleIntro: For a deposit of $2,000 ($7,000 of credit granted), fully used for 12 months then repaid, the most conservative scenario (with no reduction from yield).

exampleTable.totalBeforeYieldNote: Excluding any potential reduction from collateral appreciation

Pricing.exampleFooter: Collateral custody fees (0.5%/year) are shown and fixed at the lock, but their periodic automatic collection is not yet in service at this stage; they are therefore not included in this total. If your collateral generates a yield (gold, silver, ETH, industrial metals), part of these $1,085 may be covered automatically, within the 60% limit of the credit used (see <link>Yield</link>).

earlyRepayment.question: Are there any early repayment fees?
earlyRepayment.answer: No. You can repay all or part of the credit used at any time, with no penalty. Interest only accrues on the duration and amount actually used.

negotiable.question: Are these fees negotiable?
negotiable.answer: No, they apply uniformly to all clients at the rate in effect at the time of the lock. A future rate change only applies to new locks.

currencyDifference.question: Why does the rate differ between USD and EUR?
currencyDifference.answer: Each currency applies its own monetary reference rate (SOFR for USD, EURIBOR for EUR) before adding the same 8.5-point risk premium, hence the 1.5-point gap between the two.
